upstream.description: Compress tool outputs, logs, files, and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM. 20% fewer tokens for coding agents, 60-95% fewer tokens for JSON, same answers. Library, proxy, MCP server.

classification.analysis: Headroom is a context-compression layer for AI coding agents that shrinks tool outputs, logs, RAG chunks, and conversation history before they hit the LLM, claiming 60-95% token reduction on JSON and 15-20% on coding-agent workloads with preserved accuracy. It ships as a Python/TypeScript library, a drop-in proxy, an agent wrapper (headroom wrap claude|codex|cursor|...), and an MCP server, with a locally-run Kompress-v2-base HF model, cross-agent shared memory, and output-token reduction (verbosity steering, effort routing). Built for developers running expensive coding-agent sessions who want to cut token spend without changing prompts or losing fidelity, with Rust components and a public benchmark suite.

use_cases.title: Cut token costs on Claude Code or Cursor sessions
Compress JSON tool outputs before they reach the LLM
Wrap any coding agent with a local compressing proxy
Share compressed memory across Claude, Codex, and Gemini
